agenda_text:
This meeting will be held via teleconference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-
19 and pursuant to AB 361 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer’s Order (revised
February 23, 2022). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and
the vote will be publicly reported.

HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. Please view the meeting, which will be
live streamed at https://malibucity.org/video and https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to
submit email correspondence to mlinden@malibucity.org before the meeting begins.

HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: Members of the public may speak during the
meeting through the Zoom application. You must first sign up to speak before the item you would like
to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the Zoom conference to be
recognized.

Please visit https://malibucity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing up to speak and
downloading the Zoom application.

  Guide to the City Commission Proceedings

As a result of the Coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, the City is under a state of local emergency, as well as states of
emergency that have been declared in the County of Los Angeles, State of California, and a federal emergency
declared by the President of the United States. In order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19, the Commission
meeting will be open and public but conducted virtually because meeting in person would present imminent risks to
the health or safety of attendees. This way, the public, the staff, and the Commission will not be physically in the same
place.
The Oral Communication portion of the agenda is for members of the public to present items which are not listed on the
agenda but are under the subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. Although no action may be taken, the Commission
and staff will follow up, at an appropriate time, on those items needing response. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.
Members of the public wishing to speak during the meeting must participate through the Zoom application. You must first
sign up to speak before the item you would like to speak on has been called by the Chair and then you must be present in the
Zoom conference to be recognized. Please visit https://MalibuCity.org/VirtualMeeting and follow the directions for signing
up to speak and downloading the Zoom application.
Items in Consent Calendar Section A have already been considered by the Commission at a previous meeting where the
public was invited to comment, after which a decision was made. These items are not subject to public discussion at this
meeting because the vote taken at the previous meeting was final. Resolutions concerning decisions made at previous
meetings are for the purpose of memorializing the decision to assure the accuracy of the findings, the prior vote, and any
conditions imposed.
Items in Consent Calendar Section B have not been discussed previously by the Commission. If discussion is desired, an
item may be removed from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration. Commissioners may indicate a negative or
abstaining vote on any individual item by so declaring prior to the vote on the motion to adopt the entire Consent
Calendar. Items excluded from the Consent Calendar will be taken up by the Commission following the action on the Consent
Calendar. The Commission first will take up the items for which public speaker requests have been submitted. Public speakers
shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.
Old Business items have appeared on previous agendas but have either been continued or tabled to this meeting with no final
action having been taken. Public comment shall follow the rules as set forth under Oral Communication.
Items in New Business are items which are appearing for the first time for formal action. Public comment shall follow the
rules as set forth under Oral Communication.
Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business described above are on file in the
office of the City Manager, and available upon request by emailing MLinden@MalibuCity.org.
The City Hall phone number is (310) 456-2489. To contact City Hall using a telecommunication device for the deaf (TDD),
please call (800) 735-2929 and a California Relay Service operator will assist you. In compliance with the Americans with
Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact Yolanda Bundy, Environmental
Sustainability Director, at (310) 456-2489, ext. 229. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make
reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting. [28 CFR 35.102-35.104 ADD Title II].
I hereby certify under penalty of perjury, under the laws of the State of California, that the foregoing agenda was posted in
accordance with the applicable legal requirements. Dated this 25th day of February 2022, at 5:00 p.m.

ITEM 2.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Safety Manager Dueñas introduced Lieutenant Chad Watters. She discussed
  the COVID testing sites offered at City Hall the past two weekends. She stated the
  City would promote testing sites offered by other Las Virgenes-Malibu Council of
  Governments (COG) cities. She stated the Commission’s recommended changes to
  the parking citation fine schedule would be presented to the City Council
  Administration and Finance Subcommittee prior to going to the Council. She stated
  the City had begun promoting www.CrimeMapper.com. She discussed a grant for
  potential funding of license plate reader cameras.

  Commissioner Anneet arrived at 5:07 p.m.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores announced the County homeless count was
  rescheduled to Wednesday, February 23, 2022.

  Fire Safety Liaison Brossard provided an update on the hazard tree removal
  program. He stated the Santa Ana wind event would continue through Saturday.

  Public Safety Specialist Kaplan announced the Public Safety Expo would be held
  on June 4, 2022.

  Public Works Director DuBoux announced the next joint meeting with the Public
  Works Commission to continue discussion of Westward Beach and Measure R and
  Measure M projects would be held on Wednesday, February 23, at 3:30 p.m. He
  stated parking restrictions near Corral Beach would be presented at the next Public
  Safety Commission meeting. He stated he was discussing with the Volunteers on
  Patrol (VOP) possibly modifying the no parking times to be switched to opposite
  sides of the highway. He stated both parking projects would require a Coastal
  Development Permit Amendment (CDPA).

  Commissioner Anneet left the meeting at 5:15 p.m.

ITEM 2.C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Commissioner Spiegel discussed the first fatal collision on Pacific Coast Highway
  (PCH) in 2022. He stated he met with Todd Prince, Arson Watch, about expanding
  the role of Arson Watch with the City. He stated there were currently 84 Arson
  Watch members who are Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (LASD)
  volunteers.

  Commissioner Anneet rejoined the meeting at 5:18 p.m.

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth stated he followed up with Southern California
  Edison (SCE) about adding fire resistant insulation on wood poles, particularly
  along evacuation routes. He stated he talked to Las Virgenes Municipal Water
  District about resiliency and billing formulas. He agreed with Commissioner
  Spiegel about the great work done by Arson Watch.

  Commissioner Anneet discussed the Westward Beach project’s impact on sand.
  She stated the right-of-way extends into the sand. She stated the community would
  not support further encroachment into the sand.

  Commissioner Gibbs stated he was excited about the ignition zone grant and looked
  forward to more residents joining the program.

  Vice Chair Stewart encouraged everyone to volunteer for the homeless count. He
  thanked Public Safety Manager Dueñas for staying on top of the cameras. He stated
  having factual crime reporting would be valuable. He stated CERT was working on
  AM radio options and would report to back next month. He stated FM alerts were
  on hold. He welcomed Lieutenant Watters. He discussed an increase in fatal
  pedestrian and cycling accidents over the past year.

  Chair Frost welcomed Lieutenant Watters. He discussed fire brigade training. He
  agreed that Todd Prince brought great experience to that training. He discussed
  drug issues and LASD’s efforts to suppress them. He stated fatalities on PCH could
  be avoided with better awareness. He suggested ticketing pedestrians, as well as
  motorists. He stated Public Works staff were adding signs by fire hydrants. He
  stated parking on Point Dume at Cliffside and Birdview was out of control. He
  suggested using social media to educate about parking regulations. He discussed a
  flag presented to the fire station in memory of a Los Angeles County Firefighter
  killed in the line of duty.

MOTION  Chair Frost nominated Doug Stewart for Vice Chair. There being no further

Subject:  2022 Public Safety and Preparedness Expo

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Receive and file report on the 2022 Public Safety and
Preparedness Expo and provide feedback to staff.

DISCUSSION:  On Saturday, June 4, 2022, from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m., the City will
host the fourth annual Public Safety and Preparedness Expo (Expo) at Malibu City Hall.
Attendees can expect to see multiple displays of response equipment, vendors offerings,
and volunteer opportunities, including Malibu CERT Team, Arson Watch, Los Angeles
County Volunteer Disaster Communication Services (DCS), SoCal Fire Supply, SOS
Survival Products, and All Risk Shield.

The Expo was scheduled earlier than last year’s event, moved up from October to June,
to capitalize on early summer traffic. Additionally, the early summer date avoids
competition with school and extracurricular activities of students, as well as major events
in Malibu, such as the Malibu Triathlon and Malibu Half Marathon.

Attendees can also participate in a knowledge-based scavenger hunt by visiting the
various booths and partner agencies. Participants will need to answer three questions to
qualify to win one of several raffle prizes donated to the Expo.

COVID-19 regulations permitting, the Expo will have booths and classes inside City Hall.
Classes will vary from 30 minutes to one hour long on a variety of preparedness topics.

malibusafety.eventbrite.com.

class offerings, etc.

Subject:  Temporary Day-Use Impound Yard

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Discuss options and provide a recommendation to the City
Council regarding a temporary day-use impound yard to be used during the summer and
other peak visitor times.

DISCUSSION:  The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department (LASD) reviews and
approves towing companies for the removal and processing of vehicles that have been
impounded due to violations of local codes. Currently, Sierra Towing and Roy’s Towing,
both based in Thousand Oaks, are approved tow companies for LASD within the Malibu
city limits.

The ability to tow vehicles that are parked illegally in marked tow away zones is critically
important to managing illegal parking and public safety throughout the City. Visitors
routinely park illegally in order to more easily access the many public areas in the City.
However, this frequently creates public safety hazards and negatively impacts
neighborhoods. Unfortunately, parking tickets alone are frequently not enough to
discourage people from parking illegally.

LASD’s current ability to tow vehicles is limited by the distance tow trucks must travel to
transfer a vehicle to an impound yard, which can often be more than an hour one way.
This significantly reduces the number of vehicles that can be towed throughout the day.
By creating a day-use impound yard within the City, the number of vehicles that can be
towed is significantly increased.

  Page 1 of 3
  Agenda Item # 5.B.
 On February 3, 2021, the Public Safety Commission discussed potential locations in
Malibu for a temporary tow yard where towed vehicles could be stored until either they
were claimed by their owners or, if not claimed, transferred to the out-of-town location at
the end of the day. No vehicles would be stored at the Malibu location overnight. At that
meeting, the Commission unanimously approved the following two actions:

  • Provide a recommendation to the City Council that the new Malibu High School
  upper parking lot be considered as the preferred, primary location for a temporary
  tow yard site during the summer with the City’s properties on PCH at Heathercliff
  and/or the City Hall parking lot be considered as secondary options.

  • Form a Temporary Tow Yard Ad Hoc Committee comprised of Chair Frost and
  Commissioner Spiegel to evaluate ease of access, proximity to areas where
  vehicles would likely be towed from, environmental concerns, security
  considerations, and historical usage related to recommended locations and report
  back to the Commission, time permitting, and be prepared to make a presentation
  to the City Council.

At the March 3, 2021 Public Safety Commission meeting, the Ad Hoc Committee reported
back to the Commission, and the Commission re-affirmed its recommendation of the
Malibu High School upper student parking lot as the first choice for a temporary tow yard.

In order to implement this plan, the operator was required to obtain a Temporary Use
Permit and a Conditional Use Permit (CUP) to operate a temporary tow yard for the
summer months. On June 14, 2021, the City Council voted in favor of pursuing the
temporary tow yard at the high school and waiving the fees associated with the permits.

Unfortunately, due to the length of time required to obtain a CUP, the temporary tow site
was never implemented. It was also determined that, due to the ongoing construction at
the high school and the restrictions on the number of weekends the tow site could operate
at that location, the high school parking lot was not the best location. Ideally, a site needs
to be available from Memorial Day through Labor Day. However, the high school site would
not be available after the middle of August due to regular school activities.

Staff is now requesting that the Commission consider making a recommendation to the
City Council to use the City’s undeveloped property at Heathercliff and Pacific Coast
Highway for a temporary, day-use impound yard. The attached site map indicates the
proposed location, entrance, and exit. The tow companies using the site would be required
to use pans or other protective devices to prevent vehicle fluids from leaking onto the
ground. Personnel from the tow company would also need to be onsite to collect the
impound fees and release the vehicles to the owners.

If the Commission recommends using this site as a day-use impound yard, staff will pursue

 an amendment to the Temporary Use Permit ordinance to allow for this activity without
having to seek renewal every two weeks.

II.  NOTEWORTHY INCIDENTS

  A robbery was reported in the 23400 block of Civic Center Way. The victims were
  sitting in their vehicle charging it at the Tesla charging station when approached
  byBy the suspects. Both suspects had firearms and demanded the victims’ property.
  Property stolen were two iPhones, cash and credit cards. (22-00449)

  A robbery occurred at the 4200 block of Avenida De La Encinal. The victim and his
  girlfriend were in the area looking for a hiking trail. The victims were approached by
  the suspect (male Hispanic, 35 years, 5’8”, 180 pounds) who stated the victims had
  to pay him money for being in the area. The victim and the suspect began to argue
  and the suspect grabbed the victim’s sunglasses and assaulted him. (22-00438)

  A Malibu transient was arrested for assault in the 3800 block of Cross Creek Road.

  A local transient was arrested for attempting to enter the victim’s home by pulling on
  the front door handle. (22-00025)

  A transient from Malibu was arrested for theft in the 3800 block of Cross Creek Road.
  The suspect entered the location and began to look at store items (glasses). The
suspect
  asked for assistance from an employee. The suspect was distracting the employee while
  a second suspect (male White, 38 to 40 years of age) stole two pairs of glasses. The
  second suspect fled and avoided capture. These suspects also committed another theft
  in the same shopping area. A t-shirt was stolen in this incident. (22-00550)

  A Malibu transient was arrested for the theft of a vehicle in the 6500 block of Westward
  Beach Road. The victim had parked the vehicle at the location, locked it but had left
  the spare key inside the vehicle which allowed the door handles to unlock when pulled.
  The suspect approached the vehicle, opened it and attempted to drive away with the
  vehicle. The victim saw the suspect inside his vehicle and ordered the suspect to exit

MINUTES
  MALIBU PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  MARCH 2, 2022
  TELECONFERENCED VARIOUS LOCATIONS
  -

  5:00 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and fully teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Frost called the meeting to order at 5:01 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Chris Frost; Vice Chair Doug Stewart; Commissioners Daphne Anneet
  (arrived at 5:04 p.m.), Keegan Gibbs, and Joshua Spiegel; and Ex Officio Member Brent
  Woodworth

  ALSO PRESENT:  Susan Dueflas, Public Safety Manager; Rob DuBoux, Public
  Works Director; Sarah Kaplan, Public Safety Specialist; Gabe Etcheverry, Fire Safety
  Liaison; Luis Flores, Public Safety Liaison; Arthur Aladjadjian, Public Works
  Superintendent; Brandie Ayala, Senior Administrative Assistant; Parker Davis, Media
  Technician; Lieutenant Chad Watters, Los Angeles County Sheriffs Department; and
  Mary Linden, Executive Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Lieutenant Joseph Fender led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Chair Frost moved and Commissioner Gibbs seconded a motion to approve the
  agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Executive Assistant Linden reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted
  on February 25, 2022.

ITEM l.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Ryan Embree discussed the joint meeting with the Public Works Commission. He
  stated the Public Works Commission considered matters outside of its
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of March 2, 2022
Page 2 of 9

  jurisdiction. He stated traffic engineering was the duty of the Public Safety
  Commission. He discussed bike lanes adjacent to diagonal parking.

  In response to Mr. Embree, Chair Frost explained that the City Council directed
  the Commissions to consider the project together at a joint meeting.

ITEM 1.B.  STAFF UPDATES

  Public Safety Manager Dueflas discussed the recent County homeless count. She
  stated official results were not expected before the summer. She stated the City
  was invited to submit an application for funding for a program that would provide
  rebates to residents who implemented recommendations from a home hardening
  assessment. She discussed a meeting today with the State Office of Emergency
  Services (Ca1OES) regarding potential reimbursement for response to storms
  earlier this year. She discussed the status of flock cameras. She stated the process
  could begin while the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was being
  finalized.

  Fire Safety Liaison Etcheverry discussed the home hardening rebate program. He
  stated live fuel moisture was still over 180 percent. He stated the City received its
  first Beacon Box, which was installed at Big Rock. He discussed problems with
  locations for further installations. He discussed the status of the Mountains
  Recreation and Conservation Authority (MRCA) grant and hazard tree removal.

  Public Safety Liaison Flores discussed the homeless count and thanked the
  Commissioners who volunteered.

  Public Safety Manager Dueflas announced that Fire Safety Liaison Chris Brossard
  left the City last week. She stated the City was recruiting for his replacement.

  Public Works Director DuBoux thanked everyone for their participation in the
  joint meeting. He stated he would present the recommendations to the City
  Council at its March 28, 2022 meeting. He stated the City’s maintenance crews
  were ready to respond to rain forecasted over the next few days.

  Public Works Superintendent Aladjadjian announced upcoming  Caltrans
  pavement repair work between Webb Way and Corral Canyon Road.

ITEM 1 .C.  COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

  Commissioner Spiegel discussed observations of souped-up cars and reckless
  driving in western Malibu. He requested additional Sheriff’s enforcement. He
  discussed a fatal accident on Malibu Canyon Road that was the result of reckless
  driving. He welcomed Lieutenant Fender.
 Malibu Public Safety Commission
Regular Meeting
Minutes of March 2, 2022
Page 3 of 9

  Ex Officio Member Woodworth discussed an article in today’s Los Angeles
  Times about fire insurance relief initiated by the State Insurance Commissioner.
  He stated homeowners can truly benefit from an ignition zone risk assessment. He
  discussed fire brigade communication testing. He discussed an article in The
  Malibu Times about the Woolsey Fire. He recommended the Commissioners
  review the independent study done on the response to the Woolsey Fire. He
  welcomed Lieutenant Fender. He thanked the Sheriff’s Department and California
  Highway Patrol for their efforts to enforce street racing.

  Chair Frost agreed with Ex Officio Member Woodworth about the fire insurance
  relief offered for home hardening.

  Commissioner Anneet discussed the Russian invasion of Ukraine. She stated
  many issues suggested in the Safer From Wildfire Framework could be addressed
  at this summer’s Public Safety Expo. She expressed àoncern about dangerous
  driving on canyon roads, especially as summer approaches.

  Commissioner Gibbs left the meeting at 5:24 p.m.

  Vice Chair Stewart congratulated Lieutenant Fender for being named Acting
  Captain at the Malibu/Lost Hills Station. He stated the joint meeting was very
  successful in finding consensus so something could be done. He discussed the
  status of AM radio and FM Alerts to alert and advise. He suggested KBUU test
  the concept. He requested staff’s assistance in getting the booster antenna
  installed at Bluffs Park. He stated the homeless count was enjoyable and
  informative. He agreed accident levels and speeding were a serious concern. He
  stated Chris Brossard would be hard to replace. He commended Fire Safety
  Liaison Etcheverry for the work he did. He encouraged everyone to attend Coffee
  with a Cop. He stated he attended the installation of the beacon box on Big Rock.
  He offered his assistance with finding locations for the remaining beacon boxes.

  Chair Frost agreed that Chris Brossard had been a great asset to the City and
  would be missed, He discussed the increase in car clubs, racing, and speeding. He
  stated the fatal collision in Malibu Canyon last weekend was unnecessary and
  charges should be filed. He discussed trucks and tractor trailers driving through
  Malibu on Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) and Kanan Dume Road.
